title: Release health sessions on Bun
summary: Bun.serve with release "1.0.0" and default options never produces a `sessions` aggregate (not after the sentinel, not at t+65s, not after process exit); the only session data is the single process session from processSessionIntegration, which is sent immediately as a `session` envelope with status `crashed` when the throwing request is captured (mechanism auto.http.bun.serve, handled:false), even though the process keeps serving. A node:http server DOES get request session aggregates on develop (bunHttpServerIntegration, sessions default true): with a handled captureException the `sessions` envelope arrives at the 60s flush with exited:3 errored:1, and the process session is later sent as `exited` at beforeExit; with a throwing handler the throw is an uncaught exception that kills the process, so the aggregate is flushed at once with exited:2 (the crashed request is not counted) plus a crashed process session.

title: Cloudflare Vite plugin: autoInstrumentation, option names and defaults
summary: The SDK does exactly what the develop JSDoc says, and the docs page describes a different API. `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()` with NO options auto-wraps everything: options are top-level `autoInstrumentation` / `buildTimeInstrumentation` and both default to TRUE. A plain, never-wrapped default export produced a request span; the DurableObject, the WorkerEntrypoint and the module-scope mysql query all produced child spans in the SAME trace as the request, and the unhandled route error was captured. `_experimental.autoInstrumentation` / `_experimental.useDiagnosticsChannelInjection` (the only names the docs page documents) do not exist on develop: passing them is a TS error and at runtime they are ignored, so a reader copying the documented snippet gets full auto-instrumentation by accident rather than by the flags they set. summary: Unbundled `bun run app.ts` and the bundle with `external: ["@sentry/*", "hono"]` both work: route-parameterized span names (`GET /hello/:name`, `GET /sub/item/:id`) and both route errors (main app and sub-app) captured with mechanism `auto.http.hono.context_error`. title: K11 independent re-verification (lazy module load under Bun)
summary: K11 reproduces identically on Bun 1.4.0 AND Bun 1.3.14 (the earlier claim that 1.3.14 differs does not hold). With the sentryBunPlugin bundle, a module-scope mysql connection yields the db span; createConnection inside the request (static top-level `import mysql`) yields no db span because mysql's index.js lazily requires lib/Connection.js on first createConnection, so the instrumented module first evaluates inside the request; dynamic `await import('mysql')` in the handler behaves the same. The no-SDK variant (plain `dc.tracingChannel('orchestrion:mysql:query').subscribe(...)` at module scope, mysql loaded in the handler) fires zero channel events on both Bun versions, while the same subscriber with mysql loaded at module scope fires start/end/asyncStart/asyncEnd once per query. Holding a strong reference from user code (`globalThis.__keepMysqlChannel = dc.tracingChannel('orchestrion:mysql:query')` at module scope) makes the lazy case produce the db span on both Bun versions, which confirms the mechanism and is a user-side workaround; the SDK-side fix is to retain the channel objects it subscribes to (e.g. a module-level Map/Set of bound channels).

title: deno compile binary with the hook
summary: develop: works. deno compile (type-check on) succeeds with the SDK installed from tarballs into a real node_modules. The compiled binary behaves exactly like deno run: the hook injects mysql inside the binary (__SENTRY_ORCHESTRION__ = {runtime:["mysql"]}), GET /db gets a nested db SELECT span, /error produces an unhandled event (auto.http.deno) with a context line, /log delivers a log, and the binary works from a directory without node_modules. Sizes: 160M with all ten tarballs, 99M with the minimal set (deno + core + server-utils + server-runtime-injection + mysql; denort base is ~70M). Only difference: stack-frame paths point to Deno's compile vfs. The earlier failure came from symlinked node_modules, which deno compile embeds as 0B. compile.log: Embedded Files node_modules/ (100.23MB), -rwxr-xr-x 168217154 app; run-binary.log: injected at startup: {"runtime":["mysql"]}; drive-binary.log: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /db","spans":["db SELECT FROM users"]}, {"type":"event","exception":"route boom","mechanism":"auto.http.deno","handled":false,"hasContextLine":true}, {"type":"log","items":["info: hello from deno"]}; diff vs deno run baseline after normalizing ids and paths: NO DIFF Repro: cd $S/deep/D16-rerun/develop; npm install $S/pack/ .tgz mysql@2; deno check main.ts; deno compile --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys --output app main.ts; ./run-phase.sh binary ./app , files in $S/deep/D16-rerun/develop/ (main.ts, deno.json, package.json, drive.mjs, run-phase.sh, app, compile.log, run- .log, drive-*.log); minimal variant in $S/deep/D16-rerun/develop-minimal/ .
